title: State a negative so a reader can check it
ground: A sentence saying "no opinion carries a drafter’s name" is a claim a reader has to take. A counter named `named`, declared, incremented by nothing, and printed, is the same claim in a form they can watch fail to move.
task: Find a negative claim in your own work — something you assert is absent. Build the instrument that lets a reader verify the absence without trusting you, then write 200 words on why the sentence was not enough.

rubric.test: Can a reader operate it without reading the source?
Is there a path by which the number WOULD change? A counter nothing could ever increment proves nothing.

rubric.band: The prose does not repeat the instrument
rubric.test: Does the writing say something the counter cannot?
